mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase does not correlate with subsequent GDP contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real estate activity (HOUST) below 1,000 units signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST decline does not correlate with subsequent GDP contraction.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% YoY signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which typically leads to lower borrowing costs and increased investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of instances following a FEDFUNDS decrease, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS decrease and subsequent positive returns is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) combined with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combined signal does not correlate with subsequent consumer spending growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real final sales (RSAFS) above a 5% YoY growth rate signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS growth does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) and a tightening monetary policy (FEDFUNDS increase) signals a potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combined signal does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.
